crumb: How I Calculate a Cash Offer
title: How a Cash Offer on Your House Is Calculated | Hampton Roads
description: The inputs behind a cash offer: comparable sales, repair costs, holding costs, resale costs and risk. Check the math before you accept any offer.
h1: How I Calculate a Cash Offer on Your Hampton Roads House
lede: Cash buyers rarely explain their numbers. Here is exactly what goes into mine, so you can check the math and compare it to any other offer.
tldr: A cash offer starts from what the house would sell for after repairs, then subtracts repair costs, holding and resale costs and a margin for risk. I show you each number. It is lower than a fully prepared listing, and you can verify every input.
service_name: How I Calculate a Cash Offer

sections.h2: Step 1: What the House Is Worth Repaired
sections.html: I pull recent closed sales near your address from REIN MLS, matching size, age, style and location, and estimate what your house would sell for once repaired and updated. I use closed sales, not asking prices or online estimates. For Virginia Beach and Chesapeake you can see neighborhood medians on this site, but I price from sales near your actual address.

I look at the roof, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, foundation, water issues, windows, kitchens, baths, floors and anything unpermitted. Where the work is large I get contractor numbers. You can tell me what you know, and a walk-through tightens the estimate.

sections.h2: Step 3: What It Costs Me to Own and Resell
sections.html:
• Holding costs while I repair and sell: taxes, insurance, utilities and financing.
  • Resale costs: commission, closing costs and transfer taxes.
  • A margin for risk, since repair costs and market timing can both come in worse than planned.

Offer = repaired value − repairs − holding costs − resale costs − risk margin.

You should expect it to be lower than a prepared listing, which is why I show you both and why you should compare the net you would keep. If your house is in great shape, the gap between my offer and the list price is mostly resale costs and risk, and listing may be better.

sections.h2: How to Check Any Cash Offer, Including Mine
sections.html:
• Ask the buyer for the comparable sales and repair estimates they used.
  • Ask who the actual buyer is and whether the contract can be assigned.
  • Ask for proof of funds and the closing company’s name.
  • Get a second opinion from an agent on what the house would list for.

See how to vet any cash home buyer.

faqs: Do you use online estimates like Zillow?
No. I use closed sales from REIN MLS and an inspection of the house.
Why is a cash offer lower than market value?
The buyer takes on repairs, holding and resale costs and risk. Those are subtracted from the repaired value.
Yes. If you have repair quotes or information I do not, send it and I will revisit the numbers.
Do you charge fees to the seller?
I do not charge a listing commission or upfront fees. Closing costs and taxes still apply.
Will you show me the comparable sales?
Yes. I will show you the sales and the repair estimates behind the offer.
Does the offer change after inspection?
I will tell you before you sign what could change it. I do not retrade without a real reason.
How long is an offer good for?
I will state the expiration date on the written offer.
No. Talk to a tax advisor or attorney about your situation.
